title: FX Spec v1 (1.8 and later)
description: One Sinua object in one pattern. Editor aid only: the runtime validator (core_engine::fx_spec, exported as resolveFxSpec / resolve_fx_spec) is the authority -- it also checks that `object` matches the pattern's family, that every `params` key is one the pattern's mode reads, and applies the glTF minor-version rule (unknown keys are errors in a file this runtime fully knows, warnings in a newer 1.x file). The oldest version the runtime reads is 1.8: 1.0-1.7 were never published, so their acceptance (and the old names 1.7 replaced -- `state`, engine-key binding targets) was dropped before the first release. What each minor added, for reference: 1.1 `states` (a lifecycle map merged over the top-level design, RFC 7396) and `bindings` (app inputs -> curated Reactive targets); 1.2 `performance`; 1.3 glow `mode`/`blend` and shedding `blur`; 1.4 `materials.liquid`; 1.5 `materials.particles`; 1.6 `materials.holographic` and particles `sync`/`audio`; 1.7 the parameter catalog's names (`pattern`, dotted binding targets, array params); 1.8 `ink` and the built-in voice-state profile. See docs/fx-spec.md.

fxSpec.description: "major.minor", 1.8 or later (the runtime's floor; 1.0-1.7 are rejected). A newer 1.x file resolves, with its unknown keys reported as warnings.

pattern.description: The visual pattern, e.g. working, metering, tracking, scanning, generating. Must belong to `object`'s family.

speed.description: Multiplier on the preset's tuned speed; frameFromFxSpec applies elapsed * presetSpeed * speed.

ink.description: FX Spec 1.8: the whole visual's opacity, 0 to 1. 1 draws it as the pattern defines it; lower fades everything, halos included. A state patches it (a voice assistant's idle typically sits below 1).

palette.description: FX Spec 1.12, `object: character` only: repaint some of the character's colours (its recipe's palette names, e.g. `shell`), as hex or DTCG colours. A slot's Light/Dark tones follow it; the rest stays as drawn. A state patches it. 1.13: role names (`primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, through the recipe's `roles`), a named palette (`"theme": "sunset"`, or the string shorthand `"palette": "sunset"`) and a `dark` variant the views pick in a dark theme.

expression.description: FX Spec 1.12, `object: character` only: the character's expression. It shapes the eyes and the resting mouth; the voice state keeps the gaze, the turn and the talking or thinking mouth. A state patches it; `null` there removes it.

color.description: A color (shorthand for { value, mix: 1 }) or the full section.

params.description: Per-state engine opts (docs/parameters.md). Runtime inputs (pointer*, audio*, history*, interrupt*, muted*, voiceStateCode, peakN) and section-owned keys (color*, gradient*, glow*, noise*, pulse*) are rejected here. FX Spec 1.7: `progress` / `segment` may be arrays.

eyeStyle.description: A character's eye style (FX Spec 1.13, design note 24): a name, or its number (0-4).

anyOf.description: FX Spec 1.7: `progress` (tracking, 1-4 values, one per ring) and `segment` (stepping, 1-24 values) as lists. One key per item (`progress0`, `segment12`) is also accepted.

states.description: Lifecycle key -> design entry, merged over the top-level design (RFC 7396: objects merge, null deletes, arrays replace). Keys are free-form; LiveKit's AgentState names (initializing, idle, listening, thinking, speaking) are the convention. A state not listed renders the top-level design.

recipe.description: 1.12: a character recipe (the format of spec/characters/*.json) for `object: character`; `pattern` equal to its `id` draws it. Every field: spec/character-recipe-1.schema.json and docs/character-recipe.md.

cosmetics.description: FX Spec 1.13, `object: character` only: cosmetics the character wears (a hat, glasses, a badge): `body` and `eyes` parts on one of its slots, in the slot's units. A cosmetic that doesn't fit a character warns and isn't drawn. File-wide. See docs/character-cosmetics.md.

silhouette.description: FX Spec 1.13, `pattern: silhouette`: which head and shoulders the dots fill. A built-in by name, or a file's own outline in a 200 × 200 box (start and end the path below the shoulders: the bottom stays open and fades) with its landmarks. File-wide. See docs/fx-spec.md.

path.description: SVG path data (M, L, C, Q, Z and their relative forms), at most 16 KB.

eyes.description: The eye line: left x, right x, y. Thinking flickers along it.

mouth.description: The mouth: x, y. Speaking waves spread from it.

wardrobe.description: FX Spec 1.13, `object: character` only (design note 25): what an end user may pick. An app applies a loadout (`{ "loadout": 1, "wear": [ids], "palette": name, "iris": name, "eyeStyle": name }`) to the file; the file's own `cosmetics` are what it wears without one.

cosmetics.description: Cosmetics to pick from (the same objects as `cosmetics`).

palettes.description: Named palettes to pick from: each the same object as `palette`.

irises.description: Named eye colours to pick from (design note 27): a loadout's `iris` names one, which colours the `iris` slot (the glossy eye). Each a colour, hex or DTCG.

dtcgColor.description: W3C Design Tokens Color Module 2025.10 color value. srgb and hsl convert exactly; other color spaces need `hex` (used as a fallback, with a warning).

mode.description: stacked = concentric copies (every renderer); blur = one Gaussian-blurred halo per element (paint-contract blur). Low power with disable: ["blur"] falls back to stacked.

blend.description: How blur-mode halos composite: additive = Canvas `lighter` / SwiftUI plusLighter / Compose BlendMode.Plus.

binding.description: Maps the app's own input value to one Reactive target (docs/parameters.md): multi-stop, either direction, one CSS keyword curve per segment, always clamped to the target's range.

input.description: The app's input name (e.g. micLevel, steps, heartRate); the engine never interprets it. Missing at runtime = binding inactive.

outputRange.description: Default: the target's range, except the per-ring `progress[0]`…`progress[3]`, which default to [0, 1] (the goal = one lap); for extra laps (up to 3) pass a multi-stop outputRange, e.g. [0, 1, 3].

bindings.description: Keyed by target, so each target is bound once and a state can override or delete (null) one. FX Spec 1.7 names the targets like the parameter catalog's paths: `glow.strength`, `noise.strength`, `gradient.strength`, `pulse.strength`, `color.mix`, `progress[0..3]`; the engine-key names (`glowStrength`, `progress0`) are errors that name the path to use.

stateEntry.description: A design override for one lifecycle state. `object` and `size` are file-wide. null deletes an inherited value.

pattern.description: The pattern for this lifecycle key; defaults to the top-level pattern.

ink.description: FX Spec 1.8: this state's opacity; inherits the top-level `ink` when absent.

palette.description: FX Spec 1.12: this state's palette override (a character); merged over the top-level `palette`. 1.13: also a palette name, `theme`, role names and `dark`.

expression.description: FX Spec 1.12: this state's expression (a character); inherits the top-level `expression`, `null` removes it.

gradientPatch.description: A state's gradient override: merged over the inherited gradient, so `stops` may be omitted.

performance.description: File-wide. The host paces frames and detects power state (iOS Low Power Mode, Android Battery Saver, or an app policy) and passes lowPower; the spec declares the cap and what to shed.

maxFps.description: Frame-rate cap the host should honour. Absent = the host's default.
Cap under low power; absent = maxFps.

disable.description: Materials whose strength goes to 0 under low power (after bindings).

liquid.description: Material (1.4): the frame's dots melted into a metaball field (compact kernel), re-drawn as its iso-contours -- ink outlines (default), contour-sampled dots, or filled blobs (even-odd holes). Stateless.

strength.description: 0 = off; also the liquid ink's alpha multiplier.

reach.description: Influence radius x max(dot radius, half the median nearest-neighbour distance).

cells.description: Field grid resolution across the frame.

spacing.description: dots style: spacing x median dot diameter.

width.description: outline style: stroke x median dot radius.

keep.description: Keep the source dots on top.

blur.description: fill style: Gaussian sigma for a soft edge (paint effect).

particles.description: Material (1.5): plain ink dots emitted from the state's own dots, strokes and fills -- drifting out, flowing in, orbiting or rising, then fading. Stateless (a pure function of t + seed); composes with noise, liquid, colour, gradient, glow. Unset keys take the state's own defaults (1.6 engine: rise on rings, attract on scanning, a burst on notifying, audio-coupled drift on speaking/signal, a slow orbit on ambient orbs; see particleDefaults).

size.description: x the state's dot size (0.6 = the base radius, clamped to 0.8-1.8% of the frame; default 0.8).

spread.description: Travel distance as a fraction of the frame.

life.description: Real (wall-clock) seconds per life: the engine divides the state's preset speed back out; a spec's own `speed` still scales it.

sync.description: 1.6: 0 = staggered births; 1 = every particle born together (a burst each life).

audio.description: 1.6: couples brightness to the host's audioLevel when present (alpha x lerp(1, 0.25 + 0.75 level, audio)); positions never depend on it.

holographic.description: Material (1.6): holographic-lite -- a foil/iridescent hue sweep over each element's kept lightness, no shader. hue = hue + span x (depth x (z+1)/2 + facing x (1 - sqrt(1 - rho^2))) + 360 x speed x t, rho = distance from a view point circling the frame centre (a tilting card). Recolour only: geometry, alpha and lightness are untouched, so it has no cost and is not sheddable.

strength.description: 0 = off; how far saturation/hue move to the sweep.

span.description: Degrees of the wheel the sweep covers.

depth.description: Weight of the z (depth) term; dots only.

facing.description: Weight of the Fresnel-like distance-from-view-point term.

speed.description: Turns per second of engine time: hue drift and the view point's orbit.

transition.description: One state change (1.9): its length in seconds and a CSS keyword curve.

transitions.description: 1.9: how state changes animate. Keys: `default`, `from->to`, `from->*`, `*->to` (state keys); the most specific wins. Without it: 0.6 s easeInOut.

rules.description: 1.9: derived states. Tried in order; the first rule whose condition holds picks the `states` entry that renders. None holds: the caller's own state. A rule whose input isn't passed doesn't hold.

hysteresis.description: While already in this state, the condition is relaxed by this much, so the state doesn't flicker around its threshold.

input.description: The app input to compare (a key of the view's `inputs`).

accessibility.description: FX Spec 1.9 (docs/fx-spec.md, *v1.9: accessibility*): the view's accessible name, per-state words (they replace the name while that state shows; the app's `labels` win), and whether state changes are spoken (default true; polite and rate-limited by the engine).

name.description: The view's accessible name (over the file's `name`; the app's `label` wins).

states.description: Words per state key (any key of `states`, or a voice state). A voice state without words reads "<name>, listening".

announce.description: Speak state changes (default true). The app's `announce` option wins.
